3. Khaja Komoruddin while in possession of his share erected a shop on a part of the suit plot with the knowledge of other heirs of Golam Mohiuddin and had been possessing the same for more than statutory period of limitation. Komoruddin died leaving 2(two) wives Tohurunnessa and Maher Afjan, 6(six) sons namely, Khaja Bosir Uddin, Khaja Saif Uddin, Khaja Tayebuddin, Khaja Hafezar and plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 and daughter Zohura Khatun, who inherited the property left by Komoruddin as per their share. During revisional survey, MRR Khatian recorded in the name of the plaintiffs but share has been wrongly recorded against their names. MRR Khatian is wrong, 0.8338 satakas ought to have been recorded in Plot No.1709 and 0.0475 in Plot No.1712. The suit property has not been partitioned among the co-sharers by metes and bound. When the plaintiffs demanded partition of the property, the defendants were killing time on various pleas and finally on 1-1-1994 they denied partition of the property hence, the present suit for partition. 

 9. In support of his such submissions he submits that in MRR Khatian name of the plaintiffs are appearing though the quantum of land has been shown wrongly. It is also argued that had there been any amicable partition among the co-sharer of Plot No.1712, MRR and present khatian ought to have been stood recorded in the name of Hafezer Rahman or his heirs but no such record of right could be submitted by the contesting defendants to show that their predecessor got the property by amicable partition among the heirs of Komoruddin. He submits that since the record of right clearly shows that the plaintiffs and defendants are co-sharers in the suit property and in the absence of any evidence both oral and documentary, the trial court as well as the appellate court ought to have decreed the suit for partition allotting saham to the plaintiffs as per their share but both the courts below instead of decreeing the suit most unfortunately made out a 3rd case of amicable partition among the co-sharers observing that the property under Plot No.1712 fell in the share of Hafizer Rahman measuring 0.0350 sataks and in the share of Khaja Boshiruddin measuring 0.0125 sataks without any evidence. 

 11. Mr Md Nurul Amin, learned Senior Advocate with Mr Ashraful Alam appearing for the opposite party Nos.1-8 at the very outset submits that as per record of right Plot No.1709 contain 2.0275 sataks, the plaintiffs, in the schedule to the plaint mentioned the quantum of land as 1.4675 sataks. Subsequently, at the appellate stage by amendment of plaint totally deleted Plot No.1709 from the plaint by order dated 30-4-2008 making the plaint to suffer from defect of hotchpotch. He further submits that unless all the property left by Komoruddin are included in the plaint, only in respect of one plot their cannot be any partition among the co-sharers. He further submits that the plaintiffs rightly included 2(two) plots in the plaint though quantum of property shown wrongly in Plot No.1709 before the trial court but on appeal by way of amendment the plaintiffs deleted Plot No.1709 as a whole only seeking partition in respect of Plot No.1712 on which admittedly the defendant Nos.33-39 and 41's predecessor was in possession and one Khaja Boshiruddin possessing a portion of the land on the east. As such, both the courts below while dismissing the suit and disallowing the appeal concurrently found that the plaintiff No.1 while deposing before the court unequivocally admitted that the plaintiffs are not in possession in Plot No.1712 from the time of predecessor of the defendant Nos.33-39 and 41 and also admitted that the plaintiffs have been possessing their share by amicable arrangement among the co-sharers, the heirs of Komoruddin. He further submits that though in MRR khatian some plaintiffs' name are appearing but facts remain, the plaintiffs could not substantiate their claim that they as co-sharer ever possessed the suit property under Plot No.1712, moreover, admitted that in the year 1964 when the contesting defendant No.33 obtained sanction for construction of pucca shop house on Plot No.1712 from local Purashava he filed an objection which was rejected establishing that the contesting defendants are in possession of the property from the time of their predecessor Hafezer Rahman who purchased a portion of the land in the year 1957. As such, both the courts below rightly dismissed the suit holding that the plaintiffs could not prove their case and at the appellate stage gave up their claim in Plot No.1709 for partition and also admitted that the property under Plot No.1712 measuring 0.0475 sataks out of which 0-0350 sataks are in possession of the contesting defendants for more than statutory period of limitation.
